messages.author: 66537eeccf3193f3
messages.subject: gl2gds error in add.gdsn
parts:
Hi, 

I am trying to run prune SNPs with LD. I previously used the script with no problem. Only today when I reran the same script (and input files), I have this error which I've never had before.

> gl2gds(gl11, outfile=paste0("gl11_", rand, ".gds"), outpath = fp_out)  ##opening in gds format.
Starting gl2gds
  Processing a SNP dataset
  Converting SNP data to gds format
Error in add.gdsn(ans, nm[i], val[[i]], compress = compress, closezip = closezip,  :
  The GDS node "ID" exists.
In addition: Warning message:
In add.gdsn(ans, nm[i], val[[i]], compress = compress, closezip = closezip,  :
  Missing characters are converted to "".

I ran the script through my pipeline with the error message and found that the script still filtered some SNPs but the final number of SNPs passing through the filter is less than the previous run. Have anyone encountered this before?

Many thanks,
Sun

# Restart your R session (Menu > Session > Restart R)
library(dartR)
# read the help file to understand the new parameters
?gl2gds

Cheers,
Luis

Hi Luis,

Thank you so much for your reply and sorry for the delayed response. I have multiple projects and I only have time to come back to this.

What I have tried so far...
1. Updated the packages and ran gl.install.vanilla.dartR(flavour = "dev")

Error in gl2gds(platy.gl, snp_pos = "ChromPos_Platypus_Chrom_NCBIv1",  :

gl11$chromosome <- as.factor(gl11@other$loc.metrics$CHROM)
and reran

but still have the same error. 

4. I tried running the command on my raw genlight object (without loc.metrics and ind.metrics adding on or filtering being applied to) and the command ran without error. I attached my problematic dataset for you to see. I think some information has lost during the data manipulation. I tried to replace them as in step 3 but this was not the right solution. 

Many thanks,
Sun

messages.subject: Re: gl2gds error in add.gdsn
parts:
Hi Luis,

Just to update the solution of the last issue, I found that due to the package update, the function coding has slightly changed and I was working with my old script. After updating the script, everything worked fine. 

However, after fixing the script and rerunning some of the old datasets, I got a slightly different result. I found that mostly it came from the LD step, especially from gl2gds. I know this because I still have the old gds file generated from the same dataset to compare. I found that SNPs in the new gds didn't get removed in snpgdsLDpruning when the old one did. I ran a few more datasets, both ddRAD and dart, and snpgdsLDpruning never removes anything. I am wondering if this is normal or is something to do with data conversion in the gl2gds step. The only difference I found in the old version compared to the new one is that all snp.chromosome is labelled as 1 instead of 0 so I tried to do snp_chr = "1" in gl2gds but my dart data doesn't have chromosome position so it didn't work. I don't know how the older version managed to convert snp_chr to 1 because it came from the same dataset. I attached both old and new gds for you if you have time to look at what might have gone wrong. 

Thank you in advance for your time.

Regards,
Sun

messages.author: 592079bda2cb3220
messages.subject: Re: gl2gds error in add.gdsn
parts:
Hi Sun,

Can you try the following code.

Cheers,
Luis

install.packages("dartR")
library(dartR)
library(SNPRelate)
#filtering
test <- gl.filter.callrate(platypus.gl,threshold = 1)
test <- gl.filter.allna(test)
test <- gl.filter.monomorphs(test)
# using dummy names for SNP position and chromosome
test$other$loc.metrics$snp_pos <- 1:nLoc(test)
test$other$loc.metrics$snp_chr <- "1"
# converting to gds
gl2gds(test,snp_pos = "snp_pos",snp_chr = "snp_chr",outpath=getwd())
# Open the GDS file
genofile <- snpgdsOpen("gl_gds.gds")
# SNP pruning
gl_ld <- snpgdsLDpruning(genofile, autosome.only = FALSE, ld.threshold =0.1, method = "r")
# Close the GDS file
snpgdsClose(genofile)
